text:
jin: Heads-up — postmortem follow-up for last night's inference latency incident. We need concrete SLO/SLA changes, owners, and dashboard updates. Recurring pattern looks like the same tail spikes on long-context batches.

alex: Agreed. My proposal: tighten p50/p95 targets to reflect steady-state, but relax p99 slightly while we patch the batching path. Concrete numbers below. Thoughts? :thinking_face:

sarah: Put me on dashboards/alerts. We should add a separate panel for KV-cache miss rate + request length distribution. That'll help correlate spikes.

mike: Oncall notes: the incident was triggered when a burst of 10k requests with >2048 tokens hit the dedicated pool and batching backlog starved smaller requests. We saw p99 jump to ~1.8s for a few minutes.

ops-bot: Incident report: INCIDENT-2026-341 | Severity: Sev2 | Start: 2172463200 | End: 2172465600 | Primary: serving-runtime | Link: https://redwood.internal/incidents/2026-341

lina: I can own the dashboard work and alerts. ETA for a first pass: 1 week (2026-03-30). Will add:
- p50/p95/p99 latency panels (by model + route)
- request-length heatmap
- KV-cache hit ratio panel
- Alert rule: sustained p99 > 900ms for 3m :rotating_light:

alex: Suggested SLO tweaks (draft):
```
- name: inference_latency
  service: redwood.inference
  objective:
    - window: 30d
      target: p95 <= 250ms
    - window: 30d
      target: p99 <= 900ms
  measurement: realtime
```
Note: p99 new target is temporary until we roll batching fixes. We'll re-evaluate after the rollout.

jin: Action items:
- Alex: create PR with SLO change + rationale and link to postmortem (due 2026-03-28).
- Lina: dashboard + alert PR (first pass by 2026-03-30).
- Sarah: add KV-cache metric instrumentation to trace (help Lina correlate) (due 2026-03-27).
- Mike: prepare runbook update for long-context bursts, include mitigation steps and throttling knobs (due 2026-03-29).

mike: Quick question — do we want automatic fallback to smaller model variants when batching backlog exceeds X? That could reduce tail.

alex: Yes, propose policy: if batching latency > 200ms and queue depth > 100, route to compact-quant model (cost tier low). We'll need perf tests.

sarah: I'll add dashboard panels for the routing policy and queue depth. Also suggest creating a recurring 2-week review for "long-context latency" until we see 30 days of stable metrics.

jin: Owners acked: alex, lina, sarah, mike. We'll add these to the postmortem action tracker and set reminders. I'll spin up a short sync on Monday to review PRs.

lina: Ack. I'll open the dashboard PR and attach screenshots.

alex: Opening SLO PR now. Link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/slo-config/pull/482

mike: Adding runbook draft to docs: https://docs.internal/runbooks/long-context-bursts.md — ping me for edits.

jin: Thanks all. Goal: close high-priority remediation items in this sprint and get SLO/SLA updates reviewed by infra leads. If anyone needs to change ownership or timelines, call it out here. :+1:
